newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes rise late, sweet grades retain gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes rise late, sweet grades retain gains.

text.p: U.S. crudes recovered in late action, hauled up by heating oil, with domestics grades being led again by strong demand for light, sweet crudes.
Small parcels for November pipeline delivery were clinched at high prices, surprising market watchers who blamed the rally on speculative trading this month.
"People I never saw playing HLS (Heavy Louisiana Sweet) were playing it," a Gulf Coast trader said.
A late buyer for the grade paid up to $1.35 premium over West Texas Intermediate late Thursday, with another buyer seen today for 1,200 barrels per day, facing reluctant sellers.
Dec WTI/Cushing was at $24.80-90 a barrel, up 20 cents from Thursday, with the Nov/Dec WTI roll pegged at minus 10 cents against a nominal offer at WTI parity.

The rest of November business included WTI/Midland, which traded at minus five cents, down from prior positive territory at plus one to five cents, and West Texas Sour/Midland at minus $1.45 a barrel, up from minus $1.60/1.50 a barrel.
Moderate trade was seen for Dec, with attention focused mostly on Light Louisiana Sweet/St James which traded at 67 through 70 cents premium to the benchmark.
A one-year trade was reported at plus 30 cents for LLS.
In the heavy grades, Canadian imports and the government's sale of 1.1 million barrels from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) heralded a weaker market ahead.
West Texas Sour/Midland for Dec moved actively at WTI minus $1.48, 1.47 and $1.46 a barrel.
Dec WTI/Cushing Posting Plus stayed range-bound between postings plus $2.15 and $2.18 a barrel, with the Dec/Jan spread steady around 40-44 cents.
